findings.description: The identity-neutral default renderer-configuration and output fingerprints are pinned absolutely only by RenderGoldenTests.GoldenMatchesDecodedPixelsBytesDimensionsAndFingerprint, which is [SkiaNativeTheory]-guarded and therefore a single skip in the shipping/default configuration. No unguarded test pins an absolute fingerprint value (the unguarded fingerprint tests are relative: default == explicit-default through the same code path, and inclusion sensitivity). Task 12.4 regenerated the goldens and added the unguarded exact version pin, but did not add the pure (no-Skia) absolute default-fingerprint pin recommended when this residual was first raised as 12.3 TQ-12.3-02. I independently reproduced the residual on a throwaway copy: forcing AppendBadgePlacement to append unconditionally in both RenderFingerprint.cs and RendererConfigurationFingerprint.cs leaves the full default suite green (Failed 0, Passed 1491, Skipped 66, Total 1557; the 3 extra skips vs the workspace are the pre-existing PackagedPluginFact package-content tests, absent because the throwaway copy has no artifacts/ArrTags_1.0.1.0.zip). The documented matrix (docs/limitations.md V6) is accurate and the forced-native golden path does catch the mutation, so this is not a false-confidence hazard in the shipping verification matrix; it is a meaningful default-suite test-strength gap that should be tracked. The golden fixtures also use a fixed "CONFIG-TEST" ConfigurationFingerprint, so the golden render does not exercise RendererConfigurationFingerprint.Compute at all.

RenderDeterminismTests.SeparateProcessProducesTheSameArtifact spawns a real child `dotnet test` process (RenderDeterminismProcessProbe) and compares the independently written PNG bytes and SHA-256; the probe writes only to the ARRTAGS_DETERMINISM_PROBE_OUT path and never to Goldens/.

skips_checked: Default 63 skips decompose into 43 ARRTAGS_SKIA_COMPAT-guarded tests (incl. the RenderGoldenTests theory as one skip), 19 ARRTAGS_JELLYFIN_HOST_DIR-guarded tests, and 1 ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS-guarded test.
Forced-native full 20 skips decompose into the same 19 host-guarded tests + the 1 non-canonical cross-runtime test; no other skip remains.

No new skip was introduced by 12.4: the test diff adds one unguarded [Fact] (RendererConfigurationTests.SchemaAndRendererVersionsAreTheSingleCoordinatedAdvance) and extends an existing [SkiaNativeFact] body; no skip attribute changed. Pre-task baseline 1493 passed / 63 skipped / 1556 total -> post-task 1494 / 63 / 1557 (0 new skips).

The non-canonical skip is an honest missing-second-runtime limitation, not a hidden failure: NonCanonicalRuntimeFactAttribute skips unless ARRTAGS_NONCANONICAL_GOLDENS=1, and the test asserts NonCanonicalGoldenStore.Exists so enabling it without the Goldens/non-canonical set fails loudly (RendererCrossRuntimeTests.cs:126-128). Recorded as docs/limitations.md V2.
determinism_checked: RenderDeterminismTests.RepeatedRendersAreByteIdentical now renders both the V1 default (all-fields) and a non-default placement case (top-right-large) four times each, asserting Assert.Equal on raw PNG bytes, OutputHash, OutputFingerprint, and exact decoded pixel planes (CrossRuntimePixelComparator.Exact).
SkiaBadgeRenderer.Render creates a fresh SKBitmap and a fresh encoded byte[] per call (Encode -> data.ToArray()), so the repeated-render byte comparison cannot pass by aliasing a cached buffer.

PixelComparisonMode.Exact returns a failure on any non-zero channel difference (CrossRuntimePixelComparator.cs:115-118); the comparison primitive is mutation-verified: flipping one golden PNG byte fails the golden byte comparison at the exact position (mutation A).
The separate-process probe compares the parent render to a child-process render byte-for-byte and by SHA-256, and fails if the child produces no artifact.

No wall-clock, filesystem-order, network, or shared-mutable-state dependence found: source/image/metadata fixtures are deterministic, the probe output path is Guid-unique, and the observation-timestamp test explicitly proves timestamps are non-output-affecting.

summary: The task 12.4 golden regeneration is honest and well covered on its stated contract. The 9 existing default PNGs are byte-identical to HEAD and their manifest OutputHash is unchanged; only OutputFingerprint was regenerated, and all 13 committed OutputFingerprint values reproduce under the current renderer (forced-native 35/1/36 focused, 13/13 goldens exact). The 4 new anchor/size PNGs are valid, distinct, dimension/color-type/hash self-consistent, and reproduced byte-for-byte by the renderer. There is no writer, auto-update, or auto-approval path: mutating one golden PNG byte or one manifest OutputFingerprint makes RenderGoldenTests fail closed, and restoring returns it green. The single-version-advance test fails if either version alone advances (throwaway-copy V1/V2). Byte-determinism genuinely compares fresh PNG bytes, hashes, and exact pixel planes across repeats, across a non-default placement case, and across a real separate process. The skip matrix is honest and accurately documented: default 63 skips (43 native-guarded + 19 host-guarded + 1 non-canonical) and forced-native 20 skips (19 host-guarded + 1 non-canonical), with no new skips from 12.4 and the non-canonical skip a genuine missing-second-runtime limitation that fails loudly if enabled without its golden set. One MEDIUM finding remains: TQ-12.4-01, the residual absolute default output/configuration-fingerprint pin exists only in the native-guarded golden path, so an unconditional-append regression leaves the default suite green (independently reproduced) even though the forced-native run catches it and the documented matrix is accurate. That finding is a tracked default-suite test-strength gap, not a BLOCKER/HIGH, so the task is PASS_WITH_FINDINGS and ready for the next task; the four new PNGs must be included in the commit.
